replication_status: exact (authors' csdid call on the shipped data reproduces the printed coefficient and SE; R hand implementation of csdid's repeated-cross-section cells with cell-count weights reproduces it too, scratchpad/meta4/csdid_hand.R). Spec uses the authors' full-sample coding (absorbing cohort g_cm, switch-off rows kept), so CSA x y_sd_regsample must equal 3.561731. Switch-off-dropped variant in alt_switchoff_dropped (inactive).
notes: Nov 4: switch-off rows dropped (PROTOCOL 5b (d), as in Table 5): treat_var = eu_postGPDR dates adoption on the full panel (= the authors' csgvar) and run_spec.R drops the post-adoption site-waves with the indicator off (761 rows). The printed CS estimate is reproduced by the authors' code on the full sample (authors_rerun_csdid_*); with the authors' settings on this sample Stata csdid gives authors_rerun_csdid_dropoff_coef (se), the target of the option-B estimate. Treatment: EU website displays a cookie-consent mechanism (eu_postGPDR = EUWeb x ConsentMechanism). Adoption = first wave with eu_postGPDR = 1 on the full panel (= the authors' csgvar cohort cs_treatment_mins = g_cm in the prepared file: 322 EU adopters in 13 cohorts, waves 22-34; 588 never-treated sites, 445 US + 143 EU). SWITCH-OFFS: the indicator is not absorbing (761 of 2,778 post-adoption EU site-waves have it off). Nov 2 (team-lead): pending the PI's ruling between PROTOCOL (c) and (d), the spec keeps the authors' absorbing cohort (gvar = g_cm, all rows) so CSA = print; the switch-off-dropped variant (treat_var coding, 21,036 rows, CSA -21.891075) is stored in alt_switchoff_dropped and is one edit away. Rows: 21,797 non-missing. AUTHORS' CSA SETTINGS (PROTOCOL 5b (c)): csdid without ivar() = repeated-cross-section estimator; not-yet-treated controls (g = 0 or g > t; pipeline default); no covariates (dripw = difference of the four cell means); long2 only changes pre-period cells; simple aggregation weights each post cell (g,t) by the number of cohort-g rows in waves g-1 and t. csa_cells = 'rc_csdid' requests these cells and weights. did::att_gt(panel = FALSE) uses cohort row shares and gives -1.9686 for url_gdelt; did's unbalanced-panel mode gives -2.6475; neither equals the print, so 'pairs' and did's RC mode are both wrong here. TWFE counterpart on the full sample y ~ 1[wave>=g_cm] | id_web + wave_num (Table 4 reports no TWFE).
published_source: Article (Management Science 72(3), 2026) Table 4 'Callaway and Sant'Anna Estimation: Consent Mechanisms', column (2) Reach per million: 3.562 (52.298), Observations 21,797. Authors' Table2to5.do lines 117-129 (gen eu_postGPDR = EUWeb*ConsentMechanism; egen cs_treatment_mins = csgvar(eu_postGPDR), tvar(wave_num) ivar(id_web); csdid reach_per_million, time(wave_num) gvar(cs_treatment_mins) dripw notyet long2; estat simple) re-run in Stata 16.1 with csdid 1.81 on the shipped Main_Table2to5.dta: 3.561731 (SE 52.297774), csdid N 21,797; equal to the print in every digit. The printed N 21,797 is not csdid's N. Log: scratchpad/meta4/t03186.log.

alt_switchoff_dropped.status: active since Nov 4, 2026 (decision: 'go ahead' on the open items; PROTOCOL 5b (d): Table 4 drops switch-off rows as Table 5 does). Before Nov 4 the spec had gvar = 'g_cm' and treat_var = '' (all rows, CSA = print).
alt_switchoff_dropped.how_to_activate: set gvar = '' and treat_var = 'eu_postGPDR' (run_spec.R then dates adoption on the full panel = csgvar and drops post-adoption rows with the indicator off)
alt_switchoff_dropped.source: Stata 16.1 csdid 1.81, authors' call with 'if swoff==0' (scratchpad/meta4/t03186.log); R hand implementation identical
